target_customer.zh: 拥有AI智能体和团队的组织

companies.name: Graphify Labs
companies.one_liner: On-device knowledge graph engine for enterprises
companies.long_description:
Graphify builds queryable knowledge graphs from local codebases, docs, and Jira (105K+ GitHub stars, ~4.2M downloads, used in production by engineers at Rootly, Geotab, Tweddle Group, and Superagent). 

On that graph, its enterprise layer reviews every pull request and formally verifies each code change, proving the new behavior matches the old or handing back the exact input that breaks it. The graph updates itself as the code changes and keeps context instead of forgetting it, so your whole team and their coding agents work from one shared, always-current graph of the codebase instead of a thousand private threads. 

Runs fully on-premise, so no data leaves the building.

companies.name: Greypoint Industries
companies.one_liner: Manufacturing the future of autonomous swarm warfare.
companies.long_description: Greypoint Industries built LEGION, a drone swarm that identifies, geolocates, and tracks every emitter on the battlefield using the enemy’s own radio signals. LEGION enables our warfighters to precisely track previously obscured targets like jammers, command posts, and drone operators so they can proactively respond to threats instead of reacting to them.

companies.name: Grip
companies.one_liner: Physical AI for waste management
companies.long_description: Grip is a physical AI company building intelligent robotic systems for waste and recycling. Its technology combines learning-based manipulation and custom hardware to identify and pick objects from messy, constantly changing waste streams. By learning from real-world operating data, including every successful and failed grasp, Grip’s systems become more reliable and adaptable over time. The goal is to help waste operators reduce difficult manual sorting, recover more valuable material, lower contamination, and deploy automation more flexibly across different facilities and waste streams. Ultimately, Grip is building the intelligent manipulation layer for waste infrastructure, making recycling and the circular economy more efficient and scalable.

companies.name: GUILD
companies.one_liner: Making aerospace parts faster and cheaper for defense
companies.long_description:
GUILD is making aerospace parts faster and cheaper than today’s defense supply chain. We win defense contracts, automate manufacturing, and deliver to the government's door.

We’ve built an AI-native operating model for defense contracting: a company brain that connects requirements, pricing, supplier capability, compliance, manufacturing, finance, and delivery so each contract makes the next one faster and cheaper.

value_prop.en: AI-native platform for defense supply chain
value_prop.zh: 用于国防供应链的AI原生平台

target_customer.zh: 国防工业

companies.name: Gutgutgoose
companies.one_liner: Personalized probiotics, guaranteed to colonize.
companies.long_description:
Most data companies pay for their data. Ours pays for itself.
Customers send us a stool sample. We sequence it, build a metabolic model of that gut, and simulate whether each probiotic strain has an open niche it can colonize. We formulate the best candidates, then re-sequence 90 days later to see what actually took hold and what changed. Each cycle gives us the baseline gut, the intervention, and the outcome. At scale, the endgame is models that predict chronic disease years before symptoms.

companies.name: hardware intelligence
companies.one_liner: AI tools for the chips your AI runs on

companies.name: Hebbian Robotics
companies.one_liner: APIs for searching and analyzing Physical AI data at scale
companies.long_description:
We build APIs for searching and analyzing Physical AI data at scale, so providers have insight into the quality of their data, to sell more at higher prices.

We enable data providers to get on-demand signals and metrics on the quality of their data, without managing infrastructure.

Today, we help our customers evaluate data quality without training a robotics model.

companies.name: HERA
companies.one_liner: Hera catches thousand dollar errors before they hit the shop floor.
companies.long_description: Every custom part starts as a 2D drawing, and every drawing has to be reviewed before manufacturing begins. Today that means senior engineers checking dimensions, tolerances, and GD&T callouts by hand against ASME and ISO standards. It takes days, it bottlenecks release, and errors still slip through to the shop floor, where they become scrap and rework. Hera automates design review. Upload a drawing, get back every violation with the standard it breaks and where. Engineer-to-order manufacturers in aerospace, medical devices, and pressure vessels use Hera to release drawings faster and catch mistakes before they cost real money.

companies.name: hiloop
companies.one_liner: Infrastructure for recursive self-improvement
companies.long_description:
hiloop helps teams train agents for tasks where general models are not good enough. Give us a task, your current agent or model, and an evaluation. hiloop runs an autoresearch campaign across data, SFT and other post-training methods, continual learning, prompts, tools, harnesses, and systems, then returns the best verified improvement. It runs hosted or in your cloud.

We provide the research system around models: persistent memory, full experiment lineage, compute orchestration, and statistical verification. We’re starting with agent and model training, continual learning, and optimization.

Reach out to us for early access at founders@hiloop.ai.

companies.name: Hop Aero
companies.one_liner: Rocket cargo delivery to contested environments
companies.long_description: Hop Aero is building rocket cargo vehicles that deliver to contested environments hundreds of miles away in minutes. Our rockets fly point-to-point into the most austere locations at hypersonic speeds. Hop Aero's goal is to provide the U.S. and allies the asymmetric advantage that deters a future major conflict.

companies.name: Hoplite
companies.one_liner: Effortlessly deploy cloud software factories.

companies.name: Hubble
companies.one_liner: The intelligence layer for patient information
companies.long_description:
Hubble retrieves complete medical records on behalf of patients using patient-mediated access. Under a patient's HIPAA right of access, they authorize us once and we pull their full history from every provider they've seen (hospitals, clinics, labs, imaging centers), no per-provider integration or IT project required.

Getting records today still runs on faxes, patient portals, and release-of-information queues, so teams that need medical data wait weeks and get back a pile of unstructured PDFs. Hubble handles the retrieval end to end and returns clean, structured records, turning what used to take weeks into days.

We work with teams that live or die on getting patient records fast: legal (personal injury, mass tort, disability), life sciences and research, and anyone building products that need a patient's real medical history to work. Instead of standing up records infrastructure themselves, they use Hubble as the retrieval layer.

We're the team behind the AI agents at Grow Therapy and Amazon's One Medical used by millions of patients (Prabha was Grow's first PM building their AI agents, Aaron built the AI infra serving 1M+ clients).

companies.name: HyperProbe
companies.one_liner: Your coding agent writes code. Now let it fix prod too.
companies.long_description:
If your team uses Cursor, Claude Code, or Codex to ship, you've felt it: the AI is great at writing code, mediocre at debugging it. When something breaks in prod, you're back to grepping logs, adding console.logs, redeploying, and hoping the AI's guess is right.

HyperProbe fixes this. Your coding agent dynamically drops non-breaking probes into your running services, straight from your IDE. When a probe fires, HyperProbe captures and sanitises the exact variable state, feeding your agent real evidence instead of flat logs. 

This fixes prod incidents in minutes from the exact same window where agents write code, without ever redeploying to add a print statement. Under 1% CPU overhead. Automatic PII redaction. 

Built for backend teams shipping AI-written code today. Install in 60 seconds, see your first investigation in 10 minutes. That's why we call HyperProbe the runtime data layer for AI-native software.

companies.name: Illume Labs
companies.one_liner: 24/7 Personal Health & Longevity Companion
companies.long_description: Illume is a 24/7 AI personal health & longevity companion that connects your wearables, blood panels, and genomic data to text you personalized and actionable insights. We pull in your health data and fuse it into one secure model. You get daily text updates on what changed, what it means, and what to do next; conversational health Q&A like "What should I do to improve my bloodwork?"; cross-data trend detection that catches patterns individual platforms miss; and a full platform to dig deeper, explore your health data, and text your Illume agent anytime. We're 3 MIT grads & friends, with experience at Windsurf, MIT CSAIL, Eli Lilly, & the Broad Institute.

companies.name: IMPACT Drones
companies.one_liner: Air Defense as a Service for Civilian Infrastructure.
companies.long_description: IMPACT builds autonomous interceptor drones that ship in a sealed box. The box sits at the site it protects (data centers, power grid, airports, bases) with no crew on the pad. When sensors cue a hostile drone, an interceptor pierces its own frangible lid, launches, and rams the target, guided by onboard visual navigation that keeps working when GPS is jammed. Legacy effectors cost $1M+ per shot against $30k threats; our interceptors cost like the threat and launches scale with the swarm. Sites subscribe to protection instead of buying missiles: hardware, reloads, and monitoring included. Air defense as a Service.

companies.name: Induction Labs
companies.one_liner: Building intellectually curious AI
companies.long_description:
We are scaling foundation models that are curious about the world.

We’ve seen general intelligence appear exactly once, and its hallmark has been curiosity: a dissatisfaction with what we already know about the world, an ability to learn from world experience, and a disposition to share knowledge with other individuals. Across generations, these human traits have built modern science, technology, and culture.

We think superintelligence will come from models that work the same way: learning from their own observation, updating as they go, growing what they know. These models will start from what humanity knows and discover past us.

We believe that scaling curious intelligence is a defining problem of our time. If solved, we will live to see a new era of technological advances, scientific understanding, and human flourishing.

companies.name: Inkbox
companies.one_liner: Let your agents communicate via email, phone, iMessage, & Agent2Agent
companies.long_description: For your AI agents to behave like teammates, we give them persistent identities with their own email, phone, and iMessage. We also provide them an agent-to-agent channel, so they can communicate for task delegation.

companies.name: Instance
companies.one_liner: Automated evals for robot policies
companies.long_description:
We’re automating robot evaluation– the loop where you wait for your robot to roll out, judge its success, and then reset the scene. We're starting with step one: a success detector that automatically tells you whether your robot actually completed its task along with detailed subtask breakdown. 

We're MIT computer scientists & friends since middle school, with backgrounds at NASA JPL, SpaceX, and AWS.

Book a demo with founders@instancelabs.ai.

companies.name: Instaplay
companies.one_liner: AI-Native Social Platform, Starting with Games

companies.name: Insurf
companies.one_liner: The AI-Native Decision Infrastructure for Health Insurance
companies.long_description: Insurf is the AI-native data and decision layer for health insurance. Our first product, Inveto, automatically turns denied healthcare claims into source-cited, physician-attested appeals, recovering revenue practices lose today. Every claim it resolves builds the coverage-decision graph, the proprietary dataset of real payer behavior that powers our next product, Surely, which prices the true cost of a health plan for employers and brokers.

companies.name: Isengard Industries Inc
companies.one_liner: Mass-produced AI strike systems and Counter-UAS
companies.long_description:
Isengard Industries is not another drone company.

We build sovereign production: the means for allied nations to make precision-strike and counter-drone systems by the thousand, on their own soil, at a fraction of what the primes charge.

We call it Weapons of Mass Production. The Arsenal of Democracy, rebuilt for the drone age.

More to come, and only where it helps. You know how to reach us.

companies.name: Jcode
companies.one_liner: 20x more coding agents, 20x more productivity
companies.long_description: We make an open source low ram coding agent that enables extreme parallelization for coding tasks. Our coding agent produces SOTA results on coding benchmarks.

companies.name: Kara
companies.one_liner: Making diamond an engineering material
companies.long_description: We grow high-purity diamond wafers for advanced hardware. Used in data centers, aircraft, spacecraft, RF electronics, power devices, and lasers, our diamond moves heat up to 5× better than copper, helping critical systems run cooler, faster, and more reliably. Diamond has spent centuries as a symbol. We are turning it into infrastructure.

companies.name: Kebra
companies.one_liner: Make your field service company AI-native
companies.long_description:
Field technicians are bad at documenting their jobs, which paralyzes the back office. Kebra ends that.

We capture what happens in the field and collect the exact job details the back office needs. Before the truck leaves the driveway, Kebra turns every job into complete notes, filed warranty claims, parts orders, and follow-up sales opportunities.

Over time, every job feeds your Company Brain, so your best technicians’ expertise never leaves the company.

companies.name: Lamb Labs
companies.one_liner: World's fastest AI models
companies.long_description: Lamb Labs is building custom chips for AI inference and the world's fastest LLM model at the lowest power. We've developed a new post-training technique that converts existing models to a diffusion-based architecture that delivers 2× faster inference on existing GPUs. We then build the hardware, custom silicon chips targeting up to 20,000+ tok/s and a 63× higher intelligence per watt.

companies.name: Last Accounting Company
companies.one_liner: Agent-native accounting firm.
companies.long_description:
Last Accounting Company (LAC) is a full-stack AI accounting firm. We sell the same service (bookkeeping, tax filings, etc.) as a traditional accounting firm, but underneath agents handle everything and a certified accountant signs off. Our service is faster, cheaper, and fully integrated, allowing our clients to focus on what matters, not accounting admin.

LAC replaces both outsourced accountants and legacy accounting software for startups and SMBs. Our system is fully proprietary, from the general ledger to the accounting agents. This allows us to create powerful self-reinforcing loops and ultimately provide a state-of-the-art accounting service.

companies.name: LATO
companies.one_liner: Agent-native research and simulation platform for investors
companies.long_description:
The best investments come from conviction, and conviction comes from understanding a market deeply: its customers, its competitors, and where it's heading.

Today that understanding is slow and expensive to build. Reaching the right people takes weeks, a commercial study costs $300k+, and each one starts from scratch.

LATO does this research end-to-end, combining public data and the fund's own knowledge with first-hand interviews of a market's customers, experts, and operators. This research grounds a simulation of the market to predict how market participants behave.

companies.name: LemonLime
companies.one_liner: No-code AI that learns your business and self-creates automations.
companies.long_description:
LemonLime enables any business to deploy custom AI automations in minutes.  

It connects to your existing tools to pull information across sources, studies your business, and instantly creates specialized agents designed to support your team across departments.

Don't know where to start? LemonLime automatically surfaces suggested automations that can be implemented with a single click.

companies.name: Levocred AI
companies.one_liner: AI for credit funds, fintechs and banks
companies.long_description: Levocred AI is an AI-native platform for credit funds, fintechs and banks to automate workflows like back-office tasks, portfolio monitoring, compliance and underwriting. Live across multiple credit teams, running ~$1Bn in receivables through the platform.

companies.name: Libra Robotics
companies.one_liner: Multi-robot collaboration for harsh environments on Earth.
companies.long_description:
We build collaborative robot squads for solar farm construction.

High labor costs, labor shortages, and unpredictable productivity make infrastructure difficult to build in places that are remote, harsh, or empty. We are building robots to unlock places once considered too difficult to develop. Solar is our first proving ground, spanning utility-scale, commercial and industrial, community solar, agrivoltaic, and other projects.

Unlike solutions that automate only one task, or even part of one, we cover the workflow after PV module pallets arrive on-site: transportation, installation, alignment, and fastening. Each robot has a specific role, and fleets can be configured based on each project’s cost and schedule requirements.

Our robots operate autonomously with remote supervision. One person can supervise 4+ robots through a screen and an e-stop button, without being physically present or teleoperating them. Our robotic fleet has also been tested at night, paving the way for 24/7 operation.

We work directly with EPCs through a Robotics-as-a-Service model, requiring no robot purchase or large upfront capital investment. We also work with racking and PV module manufacturers to certify compatibility and give customers confidence in deployment.

Purpose-built hardware, multimodal sensing, and physical AI software help our robots handle real-world construction uncertainty.

companies.name: Litmus
companies.one_liner: Run an async work trial on every engineer you interview.
companies.long_description: Litmus is the most accurate read on how an engineer actually builds. We evaluate candidates through async technical assessments built from your own tech context (repos, tickets, and job descriptions), generated from scratch and scoped as real end-to-end features. Candidates work in their own setup with all their tools including AI, while we track and evaluate their process and output. Every submission runs in a sandbox, and grading is tuned to your company across tool fluency, process, and outcome. You get a real read on how someone actually builds, not just how they interview.

companies.name: Locke
companies.one_liner: Builders of the first AI-native government affairs firm.
companies.long_description:
Locke is an applied AI company changing the way companies and governments work together. 

Our first focus is building Locke Government Affairs, an AI-native government affairs firm helping early-stage companies monitor regulations, lobby policymakers, and win government contracts.

companies.name: Luca IQ
companies.one_liner: API First Tax Calculator for CPAs
companies.long_description: Luca IQ is an API for deterministic tax calculation and an IRS Authorized e-filing engine - the foundation for accounting firms and fintechs building on tax.

companies.name: Lumeria
companies.one_liner: Oura Ring for Skin.
companies.long_description: Your skin is yours, but understanding it has never felt that way. Getting answers has meant an appointment, a price, and a long trial-and-error process. We're changing that. Lumeria puts your skin in your own hands: the power to see it, know it, and own its story yourself, at home and on your terms.

companies.name: machine0
companies.one_liner: Cloud computers for AI agents
companies.long_description:
machine0 is a CLI for agent compute: `machine0 new mybox` gives your agent a full cloud VM, billed by the minute, from small up to 60 vCPU / 240 GB and 8×H100s. Agents drive it themselves via CLI or MCP.

Agent workloads are moving from ephemeral to always-on. A coding agent working on a hard feature runs 6-8 hours. Auto-research agents run for days. machine0 is the environment in which these agents run.

companies.name: Maingen
companies.one_liner: RL environments for industrial operations
companies.long_description: Maingen builds RL environments for industrial operations ($5 trillion slice of the US economy) so frontier labs can train models that actually run factories.

companies.name: Manifold
companies.one_liner: Low-cost, deployment-ready robotic labor for warehouses
companies.long_description:
The US Warehouse industry spends $75bn on labor each year. Yet, only 10% of US warehouses have any form of automation, because existing robotics are too expensive and hard to integrate. 

Manifold deploys autonomous robots that handle picking, loading / unloading, and palletizing — priced by pick. Integration in hours. No upfront costs. No retrofitting. No need to rebuild the operation around the robot. 

Our mission is to make it easy for any warehouse to adopt robotics.

companies.name: Marble
companies.one_liner: The autonomous back-of-house for restaurants.
companies.long_description:
Marble is the first AI-native operating system for the restaurant back-of-house. 

Restaurants, cafes and bars still run on a patchwork of disconnected point solutions, spreadsheets, clipboards and tribal knowledge, which costs the industry billions each year in stockouts, food waste, and lost profit. 

Marble replaces that entire stack with one system. Computer vision and voice AI capture real-time inventory levels 90% faster than manual counts, ML models forecast item-level demand at 97% accuracy, and AI agents run dozens of end-to-end workflows autonomously, from procurement and invoice reconciliation to scheduling, food prep, menu engineering, and more.

companies.name: Marengo
companies.one_liner: Automating engineering design, starting with data centers.
companies.long_description:
Marengo designs data centers at double the speed and half the cost with AI. We’re working with some of the largest data center builders in the world to improve how design is done today.

We're backed by Y Combinator, a16z & Index Venture Scout Funds, as well as investors/angels in OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX, and more.

Our advisors include the former President & CEO of Saipem America ($3B+ P&L), former President of Exyte's Advanced Technology Facilities GBU ($6B+ P&L) and more.
companies.funding_mention: We're backed by Y Combinator, a16z & Index Venture Scout Funds, as well as investors/angels in OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX, and more.

companies.name: Markov
companies.one_liner: Data for computer-use ai
companies.long_description: We source high quality tasks and data to train the next generation of computer use AI models.

companies.name: Mireye
companies.one_liner: Infrastructure for Physical World AI Agents
companies.long_description:
AI agents are starting to act in the real world, but they can't reliably understand it. 

Every fact about a place has its own silo: land in GIS maps, power in utility portals, people in census tables, policy in county PDFs. All built for humans, none for agents. Underneath, the data is fragmented across thousands of sources, unstructured and complex.

Mireye is building the infrastructure that powers agents to make decisions and act in the real world. One API and MCP to connect agents to the physical world with accurate data enrichment, signals and tools.

Our mission is to index every inch of the earth, and make it as queryable as the web.

companies.name: Molagri
companies.one_liner: Resistance free pesticides.
companies.long_description:
Molagri develops safer, more effective pesticides for agriculture.

We design biopesticides that hit a precise molecular target unique to pest insects, knocking out pests while sparing pollinators, beneficial insects, and the wider ecosystem. By modeling how pests are likely to evolve, we stay a step ahead of resistance, keeping our products effective against the pests of today and tomorrow. The higher efficacy and biobased production will also contribute to emissions reductions in both manufacturing and field use.

Our founders are PhD lab mates from the University of Toronto who have worked together for six years and published in Nature Communications and Nature Microbiology.

companies.name: Mosaic
companies.one_liner: Defining the frontier of multiplayer AI.
companies.long_description:
Mosaic's main product, Ocean, gives people and their coding agents shared memory across every session, so everyone can understand what happened, why decisions were made, and pick up where someone else left off.

We also built Mosaic, a real-time coding environment where multiple people and their agents can work together live. It went viral, defined the multiplayer AI category, and inspired frontier labs like Anthropic.

Together, we’re building the infrastructure for people and agents to share context and work together.

companies.name: Moving Atoms
companies.one_liner: Virtual Reality for Evaluating Robots (World Models)
companies.long_description: We use World Models to evaluate  and train robots. This enables you to test your policy checkpoints easily, as well as augmenting your training dataset. Scaling GPUs is much cheaper than scaling robot arms and humans needed to moniter them.

companies.name: Nebula Security
companies.one_liner: Building Mythos for everyone
companies.long_description:
Nebula Security is an AI-native cybersecurity company founded by world-class hackers.

Nebula Security provides Mythos-level cybersecurity reviews and product security auditing, conducted by our state-of-the-art AI agent and world-class hackers themselves, covering everything from code-level vulnerabilities to architectural weak points.

We were the first team to build an nginx RCE and the first to root Android 17. Our co-founders include members of the world’s No. 1 CTF team, DEF CON winners, Black Hat speakers, and PhD in cybersecurity. We have won $400K in bug bounties by exploiting the Linux kernel and Chrome browser.

“Audited by Nebula Security” is a mark of serious security credibility: a signal to customers, investors, and partners that your product has been reviewed by the world’s best hackers.

companies.name: Neuromorphic
companies.one_liner: Building embodiment agnostic robot brains.
companies.long_description: Neuromorphic is building an embodiment-agnostic “brain” that makes robots fast to deploy and easy to manage through natural interfaces like Slack, email, and phone. Our goal is to make deploying robots in wet labs and other physical industries as easy as onboarding a new employee.

companies.name: Neuron Industries
companies.one_liner: Industrial Controllers built for AI
companies.long_description: Neuron is crafting the world’s first purpose-built industrial controller for AI, replacing the antiquated PLCs running every machine and factory. We help customers from chemical processing to nuclear reactors compress controls projects from weeks to hours.

companies.name: Nex
companies.one_liner: Claude Cowork for GTM Automations
companies.long_description: Nex turns your GTM goals into complex GTM automations only the world's best GTM engineers know to build, across 1000+ integrations. Instead of just chatting, the agent writes code as it works to make workflows deterministic, fast, and cheap to re-run, and delivers real output: a Slack message, an opened PR, or a live structured data table. Built for teams.

companies.name: Nori
companies.one_liner: Affordable robot you can teach to do anything
companies.long_description:
Nori builds home robots that cost less than $2,000 and that anyone can teach. Out of the box, the NORI L3 does household chores: loading the dishwasher, folding laundry, tidying up. But because anyone can train it, it also learns your specific tasks, like washing paintbrushes if you're an artist or flipping sheet music while you play guitar. It's a general-purpose robot, not an appliance.

We launched pre-orders 6 weeks ago and have already booked $100K in revenue.

Humanoid robots exist, but they cost $20,000 or more and are demoed, not shipped. We got to $1,688 without sacrificing capability. Instead of expensive actuators, we use low-cost servos and get more out of them through smarter control and design. A wheeled base with a lift gives full floor-to-counter reach without the cost and fragility of legs, and we streamlined manufacturing from day one, assembling in the US.

The teachability is the moat. Every skill a user trains can be shared, so each customer makes every robot more capable. Hardware is the entry point; the skill ecosystem is the recurring revenue.

We're robotics researchers from Columbia labs like RoboPIL (robot learning) and CGUI. Working with $100K research robots that struggled with everyday tasks convinced us the problem isn't capability, it's cost. Good robots don't need to be expensive.

Households already spend $2,000+ on single-task machines: a dishwasher, a washing machine, a vacuum. We sell one robot at $1,688 that does the work of all of them and learns more. At 5% of US households and $25 a month for skills, that's $2B a year in recurring revenue, on top of hardware.
companies.revenue_mention: $100K in revenue

companies.name: Olam Labs
companies.one_liner: Building multi-agent simulations for model evals and training.
companies.long_description:
There is a massive shortage of genuinely good AI evaluations. Multi-agent environments are an underdeveloped way of evaluating models that we think will help address our increasingly worse shortage of evals. We're starting with Multi-Agent Arena, where anyone can come compete against frontier AI models in social multiplayer games, as we build towards the full stack for multi-agent environments. 

Try Multi-Agent Arena at https://olamlabs.ai/ :)

companies.name: Omanta
companies.one_liner: A research lab for one
companies.long_description:
Omanta is a personalized research lab for patients who have exhausted standard options, want to prepare proactively for recurrence, or are living with an unresolved diagnosis.

We direct the full operational infrastructure, personnel, expertise, and technology of a large research program toward understanding and addressing the challenges of individual patients across oncology, rare disease, and undiagnosed conditions.

For clinicians, we act as a collaborative partner, providing a living roadmap for ongoing patient care built on a rigorous and evolving scientific evidence base.

We fully operationalize patient-specific research programs, covering tissue logistics, diagnostic follow-up, data integration, multiomic analysis, therapeutic strategy development, and more.

Omanta brings context and clarity to complex cases, helping clinicians see more of the scientific picture as they decide how best to care for their patients.

companies.name: OneCLI
companies.one_liner: The Identity Gateway for AI Agents
companies.long_description:
OneCLI is a credential isolation gateway for AI agents. Agents see placeholder tokens instead of real API keys and OAuth credentials, the real secrets are injected at the network layer, so a compromised or misbehaving agent can never leak them. 

Teams get per-agent access control, full audit logs, and one-click integrations with Gmail, GitHub, Jira, Slack, and 50+ other apps. OneCLI is open source (2.5K+ GitHub stars, 300K+ downloads), Already the default credential layer for products like NanoClaw.

companies.name: Ooak Data
companies.one_liner: We build the world's largest library of real-world business workflow…
companies.long_description:
The promise of AI agents is still unmet in complex, real-world business environments. Our mission is to make it possible for agents to reliably accomplish concrete and useful tasks.

That’s why we're building **Alexandria,** the world's largest library of real-world business workflow datasets.

companies.name: OpenRelay
companies.one_liner: Distributed, hardware-agnostic AI inference

companies.name: OpenTrade
companies.one_liner: The new interface for investing.
companies.long_description: OpenTrade is rebuilding the trading experience for a generation raised on games, social products, and AI.

companies.name: OpenVector
companies.one_liner: AI that turns any camera to an autonomous worker with real-time vision
companies.long_description: OpenVector transforms any existing camera into an automated 24/7 workforce without requiring new hardware. Users simply describe a task in plain English, and OpenVector automatically builds a custom AI vision model to monitor the feed. When it detects an important physical event—like a stalled production cycle, a safety violation, or a waiting customer—it operates a computer just like a human to take immediate action. It integrates with legacy systems to make calls, send emails, update a POS/CRM, or trigger webhooks in real time. OpenVector enables any camera to do real work.

companies.name: Operon
companies.one_liner: Agentic data layer for manufacturing & process industries.
companies.long_description:
Operon is the data intelligence layer for heavy industry. We ingest the messy documents a plant runs on (P&IDs, schematics, datasheets, scans) and turn them into one structured, queryable model of the facility.

On top of it, engineers query their plant in natural language and build agentic workflows for safety, compliance, and design.

companies.name: Orvixo
companies.one_liner: AI advanced planning and optimisation for manufacturers.
companies.long_description: Orvixo uses AI to build reactive end-to-end planning and optimisation models for manufacturers.

companies.name: Osseus
companies.one_liner: The intelligent development platform for robotics
companies.long_description:
Osseus is the intelligent development platform for robotics. It plugs into the tools a team already uses - CAD, ECAD, GitHub, Jira, docs, messaging, and test runs - creating a live dependency graph of their entire robot stack. It automatically builds and maintains the relationships between every part, board, requirement, test, and decision.

When a hardware change is made, the map traces the downstream impact across mechanical, electrical, and software. Osseus's agents find which requirements may be compromised, run the attached tests and sims, create fixes for the affected hardware/software on branches, and re-run the tests to confirm the new design doesn’t break downstream.

Osseus includes a robotics component marketplace. Teams can list spare parts and hardware for others to buy/rent during prototyping, and designs can be evaluated against real component availability. If a part has a long lead time or is unavailable, engineers can quickly find compatible alternatives in their area instead of waiting weeks or asking around their network.

Design review also happens in Osseus. Engineers see why a design might not work, what's been tried before, and why something was built the way it was, pulled from prior conversations between engineers and with suppliers. Suppliers comment directly on a part through a secure link instead of back and forth over email, and what they say is remembered. If a supplier flags that a design isn't machinable, or that changing a feature would cut cost, that insight automatically appears the next time someone designs something similar, saving time and money.

We ultimately will use the platform's deep engineering understanding to develop physical-AI models that reason jointly over the robot's geometry, electronics, kinematics, components, software, and real-world performance so people can optimize and iterate on robots much faster. Get in touch to learn more!

companies.name: PokerClubHub
companies.one_liner: Host a Poker Club and Make Money
companies.long_description:
TL;DR: PokerClubHub is the first licensed poker club platform. We protect players’ deposits and allow anyone to open their own poker club and make money.

Regulated online poker sites like PokerStars have open player pools and thus are full of pros and bots, driving players to unregulated private clubs.

Existing poker club platforms like ClubGG have no payments processing. Players deposit with a club owner by sending them crypto for play-money chips. In theory, these chips can be exchanged back for money. However, players can get scammed and withdrawing takes ages.

This model is also broken for honest club owners who have to manually process hundreds of deposits a day. They lose out on rake when they sleep and struggle to get players to trust them.

On PokerClubhub, players deposit with PokerClubHub, not the club owner. We handle all deposits and withdrawals for the club owner, saving them time and increasing their earnings. We pay the rake (if any) to club owners as affiliate fees.

We hold the same gaming license as BetHog (built by founders of FanDuel) and Nexa Poker (part of World Poker Tour). Player deposits are secured using Fireblocks.

You can also play rake-free games with your friends and acquaintances on our platform. We ensure that everyone pays up.

Just describe what you want (a customer lookup, a dashboard, an approval flow), and Prized builds the tool on top of the right company data inside a governed boundary.

The people who feel the pain of missing internal tools most are non-engineers. They understand the workflow best but are blocked by the software layer, so they wait on engineering, duct-tape spreadsheets together, or increasingly rip company data into Claude Code and Cursor with no thought to permissions, sharing, or governance.

Prized makes security the default, enforced in the infrastructure rather than left to whoever built the tool. Each tool gets access only to the tables and integrations it was explicitly granted, credentials are workspace-scoped so tools can't cross org boundaries, and outbound calls go through a controlled layer. 

As an employee builds and shares, a teammate forks it and re-points it at their own data, and over time the company builds up a library of governed tools it actually owns.

Hudson was founding engineer at Gander (F24, acquired by Archer), then full-stack at Suno. Marinos studied CS and ME at Stanford and was on the same Gander team.

companies.name: Riften
companies.one_liner: Earned Intelligence for every company.
companies.long_description:
Riften builds earned intelligence: models that come out of a company’s own work instead of out of a lab.

One environment variable points an existing application at Riften instead of OpenAI or Anthropic. Riften routes each request to the least expensive model likely to handle it, using open-weight models we host whenever they are sufficient. Customers lower inference costs before any training begins.

Because Riften sits in the request path, real tasks and their outcomes create training evidence the company controls. Riften uses that evidence to improve routing and train private models on open weights around recurring work. Those models earn production traffic by meeting the same bar as the APIs they replace.

Over time, frontier APIs handle only the tasks that still require them. The rest runs on models the company owns, on infrastructure it controls, inside the applications where the work happens.

companies.name: Rindler
companies.one_liner: The translation layer between AI agents and the web
companies.long_description:
Rindler turns any website into deterministic abstractions that AI agents can operate on with speed, efficiency, and reliability.

Rindler drives a real browser to execute tasks on websites. It signs in, handles one-time verification codes, navigates to the right screen, retrieves records or completes forms, and returns structured output in a caller-defined schema.

Most browser agents re-process and re-compute the same website every time they visit it. Rindler remembers. Our infrastructure gets faster and cheaper the more it is used, and when a site changes underneath it, Rindler detects the break and heals itself.

For operations leaders, Rindler takes on the repetitive website work your team does by hand, giving them their time back for the work that matters.

For agent builders, Rindler is a single endpoint that carries out tasks on the web, so you do not have to build or run browser infrastructure of your own.

companies.long_description:
Geopolitical conflicts and natural disasters frequently expose the vulnerability of the American chemical industry. The reason? Production is centralized and fossil fuel-dependent. The solution? Localized production using an undervalued resource: biogas. The US produces enough biogas to make over $20 bn/y worth of chemicals, but 60% is wasted in low-margin applications or flared altogether.

Rise Reforming is commercializing a modular process to transform this underutilized biogas on-site into cheap, supply-secure chemicals. Our beachhead market is dimethyl ether (DME), used as an aerosol propellant and a low-carbon fuel additive in propane. Our target market is methanol: an established billion $ chemical and the future of low-carbon shipping.

We're doing our pilot project at a Chicagoland wastewater plant. This will be the first wastewater biogas-to-methanol demo in the Americas.

We're hiring for a senior chemical process engineer. Apply here: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/rise-reforming/jobs/wJ9Q9nv-senior-chemical-process-engineer

companies.name: Robocurve
companies.one_liner: Evaluating robots in the real world.
companies.long_description:
Robocurve builds open-source tools and independent benchmarks to measure how well robots can do real-world jobs. Instead of relying on unverified demo videos from frontier labs, we score their models on reproducible benchmarks that anyone can trust.

Today there are no well-run, standardized robotics benchmarks. Labs evaluate in-house, and no independent group has stepped in to run continuous benchmarking as a service. The result is that no one actually knows how good anyone else is, or where the real frontier sits.

Good benchmarks require operating and maintaining physical hardware and real-world setups. Simulation only goes so far, since models that look strong in sim can show large performance gaps once deployed in the real world. Building real-world benchmarks means coordinating job-domain experts, evals engineering, and hands-on robotics all at once.

Frontier labs are targeting general-purpose robotics by 2028, yet the field of robotics evals barely exists. Whoever builds the trusted measure of robot capability becomes the reference everyone relies on. We combine backgrounds in AI evals and robotics to build and grow this field as fast as possible. We already shipped v1 of our open-source framework, Inspect Robots, and ran our first pilot scoring a frontier model on a real robot.

companies.name: Hemlock
companies.one_liner: Force-sensing wristband for training robotic AI
companies.long_description:
Every serious robotics lab is bottlenecked on the same thing: demonstration data. The field has converged on egocentric video and hand pose as the substrate, and both are now cheap to collect at scale. What neither of them contains is force. A video of someone picking up an egg and a video of someone picking up a rock are nearly identical in pixel space and nearly identical in joint angles. They differ almost entirely in a quantity nobody is recording. Policies trained without it learn geometry and inherit no sense of touch.

Hemlock closes that gap at the source. Our device, the Bracelet, is a wrist-worn surface EMG band that reads the electrical activity of the forearm muscles that actually drive the hand, which means it recovers contraction force directly rather than inferring it from motion. This distinction is the whole thesis: force cannot be reconstructed downstream of kinematics, because a hand squeezing hard isometrically and a hand resting can occupy the identical pose. Muscle signal is the only non-invasive channel that separates them.

companies.name: herdr
companies.one_liner: building the open agent runtime
companies.long_description:
Developers don't run one coding agent anymore. They run fleets of them — for hours, sometimes days — across laptops, servers, and sandboxes. Keeping track of that work is the new bottleneck: which agent is blocked, which one finished, which terminal is it in, and why did everything die when the laptop closed.

Herdr is the open-source home for that work. A background server owns the agents' terminal sessions on each machine, so the work survives disconnects, closed lids, and dropped SSH. Herdr detects each agent and turns the chaos into an attention queue — working, blocked, done, across every project — so you look only when an agent needs you. Every client is just a view: the bundled terminal UI, SSH from another machine, your phone. Close one, open another; the work never stops.

Software can drive it too: a CLI, a socket API, and a plugin marketplace that passed 500 community plugins in its first month. The runtime is Apache-2.0 and stays open. Four months after launch: 25k GitHub stars, 340k downloads.
